data.name: Asmaeel
data.gender_notes: Asmaeel is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Asmaeel is the name of a son of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) in Islamic tradition. It is derived from the Arabic word 'asma' which means 'lion'. It is a name of a brave warrior who was sacrificed by his father Ibrahim at the age of three years to test his faith and obedience to God. It symbolizes bravery, sacrifice, and loyalty.
data.spiritual_meaning: Asmaeel is a name of a righteous and brave soul who sacrifices his own self for the sake of Allah. It is a name of a person who is selfless, strong, and fearless in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Asmaeel belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lion, the brave one.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Asmaeel total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: إسماعيل
in_arabic.meaning: اسماعيل هو اسم يعني سمعه الله او من سمع و استمع
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسماعيل هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و يعني سمعه الله او من سمع و استمع، و هو من الأسماء التي وردت في القرآن الكريم، و هو اسم سيدنا إسماعيل عليه السلام، ابن سيدنا ابراهيم عليه السلام، و يعتبر اسماعيل من الأسماء ذات الأهمية الكبيرة في التراث الإسلامي

in_urdu.name: اسماعیل
in_urdu.meaning: اسماعیل کا مطلب ہے اللہ کی سننے والا یا جس نے سنا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: اسماعیل ایک عربی نام ہے جس کا مطلب ہے اللہ کی سننے والا یا جس نے سنا ہے، یہ نام قرآن مجید میں ذکر ہوا ہے، اور یہ سيدنا اسماعيل عليه السلام کا نام ہے، جو سيدنا ابراہيم عليه السلام کے بیٹے تھے، اور یہ نام جنوبی ایشیاء میں مسلمانوں کے درمیان میں بہت مقبول ہے

data.cultural_impact: The story of Asmaeel is an important narrative in Islamic culture as it highlights the strong bond between a father and his child, even in the face of extreme sacrifice and personal loss. This story also serves to emphasize the importance of faith and obedience to God, and the willingness to sacrifice one's own desires and possessions for the greater good.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Asmaeel holds a deep spiritual significance in Islamic tradition as it represents the ultimate expression of selflessness and faith. Prophet Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his beloved son Asmaeel showcases his unshakable faith and obedience to God. This act serves as an inspiration for Muslims to prioritize their spiritual growth over their personal desires and to submit to the will of God in all aspects of their life. Furthermore, the sacrifices made by Prophet Ibrahim (as) and Asmaeel (as) are also symbolic of the ultimate sacrifice made by Prophet Ibrahim's son, Prophet Ismail (as), who was also the ancestor of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), and was sacrificed on Mount Arafat during the annual pilgrimage of Hajj. This story highlights the personal sacrifices made by the early Prophets and their unwavering commitment to God's will.
